chunks: And from him (al-Hasan ibn al-Faraj) from Fadala from al-'Ala' from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)

Regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted and Mighty: 'And upon those who are able [to fast, but with hardship] - a ransom [as substitute] of feeding a poor person [every day],' he said: 'The old man and the one afflicted with thirst.'
And regarding His saying, Exalted: 'And whoever is not able to do so, then the feeding of sixty poor people,' he said: 'From illness or thirst.'

key_terms.الْعُطَاشُ: Thirst or one afflicted with thirst
key_terms.فِدْيَةٌ: Ransom or compensation paid by those unable to fast

ai.seo_question: What is the difference in fidyah for those unable to fast due to old age versus illness?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the specific application of fidyah is distinguished based on the nature of the inability: the obligation to feed one poor person applies to the elderly and those with chronic conditions like persistent thirst, while feeding sixty poor people is prescribed for those incapacitated by illness or temporary thirst. This distinction highlights the Shia scholarly understanding of proportional expiation based on the severity and duration of the impediment to fasting. The hadith thus provides a nuanced legal framework for those who cannot fast but are not permanently exempt, ensuring their financial burden aligns with their specific condition.
